newsitem.title: South Korea: S.Korean 3-yr yields close up on liquidity worries.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields close up on liquidity worries.

text.p: Yields on South Korea's benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed higher on Friday on worries about tight liquidity, dealers said. off a total of 2.31 trillion won from the banking system through repurchase agreements.
New corporate bond issues were estimated at 26.1 billion won on Friday, up from 21.5 billion won worth issued on Thursday.
Dealers said the liquidity situation was expected to be eased on Saturday when the repurchase agreements would be paid back.
Three-month certificates of deposit closed unchanged at 11.70 percent, while the overnight call rate slightly rose to an average of 11.20 percent from Thursday's 11.00 percent.
